author: sjm41
body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**
ARBA00023137

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel FBgn0032752 | CG10702 (Q9VJ04)
Dmel FBgn0051431 | CG31431 (Q8IN19)


* **Description of issue**
ARBA00023137 -> keyword [Tyrosine-protein kinase](https://www.uniprot.org/keywords/KW-0829) (KW-0829)-> [protein tyrosine kinase activity (GO:0004713)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0004713)

The match with CG10702 is because of this:
InterPro signature [IPR000494](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/IPR000494) Receptor L-domain
InterPro signature [IPR006211](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/IPR006211) Furin-like cysteine-rich domain
InterPro signature [IPR036941](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/IPR036941) Receptor L-domain superfamily

The match to CG31431 seems to be a FunFam match.

However, neither protein has a kinase domain, and neither is characterised to be catalytically active.

author: Antonialock
body:
CG10702 and trio are fixed and will be released in the June 10 release (current date in the calendar....).

Q8IN19 -  This is very annoying. This protein is FGFRL1 and in Drosophila it has been assigned funfam 2.60.40.10:FF:000020 - most other species are in 2.60.40.10:FF:000016

I do find FGFRL1s in other organisms that also belong to 2.60.40.10:FF:000020 and some have been mentioned in the literature (but no functional characterization) - 
eg 
Ciona intestinalis F7BEX9 (fragment, the proper sequence is in uniparc)
c. elegans Q95XJ7 igcm-4

but experimentally characterized ones in weird and wonderful  organisms are all 2.60.40.10:FF:000016 or have no funfam assigned
eg
Branchiostoma lanceolatum C8YQD2 "amphioxus "
Dugesia japonica Q8I0V7 nou-darake (planarian)
Strongylocentrotus purpuratus D2T1S8 (sea urchin)

Since kw2go is sunsetted I will close this ticket, but because the protein has SP annotations that are wrong I will open a new ticket on our internal jira tracker so I can periodically look too see if these get published (our current policy is to only annotate published trembl entries into SP - however perhaps I really ought to pull it in by similarity, it's misleading that it has the protein name "receptor protein-tyrosine kinase" + EC....)
